lines.text: You were told a diamond means forever. That is not an ancient tradition. It was a sales line.
Before the nineteen thirties, most engagements in America did not involve a diamond at all.
In 1938, De Beers hired the advertising agency N.W. Ayer to change what the stone meant to people.
In 1947, a copywriter named Frances Gerety wrote four words: a diamond is forever.
The line ran for decades, until a written campaign stopped sounding like an advertisement and started sounding like something your family had always known.
The two months salary rule is often blamed on the same campaign. Historians dispute that part, so leave it aside.
You can still buy the ring. Just know which part was inherited and which part was sold.
